lemon-hill.description: Lemon Hill is East Fairmount Park's historic mansion and hilltop landscape, currently closed to public use during post-Fan-Festival breakdown and restoration planning.
lemon-hill.location: Use the mansion pin at 1 Lemon Hill Drive. The hill sits above Kelly Drive in East Fairmount Park and is separate from Belmont Plateau, Memorial Hall and the West Park attractions.
lemon-hill.parking: Do not drive to Lemon Hill while the park is closed. Event breakdown and restoration work can control Lemon Hill Drive, nearby park roads and curb access; choose another Fairmount Park destination until the operator lifts the closure.
lemon-hill.hours: Lemon Hill park is currently closed to the public for FIFA Fan Festival breakdown. Mansion access is also by scheduled visit rather than general park hours. Check the official page before traveling.
lemon-hill.restrooms: There is no dependable public restroom available while the Lemon Hill area and mansion are closed. Plan facilities at a confirmed-open destination elsewhere in Fairmount Park.
lemon-hill.fees: There is no general public visit while the closure is in effect. Future mansion tours or programs may require reservations or admission; use the official schedule when access resumes.
lemon-hill.accessibility: Closure fencing and work areas make the current visit unavailable. When the site reopens, confirm the mansion entrance and step-free route because a historic hilltop building and sloping grounds do not provide uniform access.
lemon-hill.dogs: Do not bring pets into the closed area. When ordinary park access resumes, the City's six-foot leash rule will apply outdoors, while the historic house may keep separate animal restrictions.
lemon-hill.family: Skip Lemon Hill as a family destination until the closure is lifted. The City has announced future playground, restoration, tree, lighting and accessibility improvements, but opening dates and finished amenities are not yet published.
lemon-hill.need: This is a real temporary closure, not simply a mansion-hours issue. Recheck the official Lemon Hill page and City improvement updates before making the hill the purpose of a trip.

belmont-plateau.description: Belmont Plateau is West Fairmount Park's broad skyline overlook and open recreation landscape, with picnic space, sports fields and connections toward the Trolley Trail.
belmont-plateau.location: Navigate to Belmont Plateau on Belmont Mansion Drive, not the broad Fairmount Park pin. The skyline lawn is in West Fairmount Park, north of the Mann Center and west of the Schuylkill River.
belmont-plateau.parking: Use legal spaces serving Belmont Mansion Drive and the plateau, then follow posted event restrictions. Roots Picnic and other large events can close roads, reserve lots and change rideshare or pedestrian approaches.
belmont-plateau.hours: Use the open lawn and trail connections during daylight; City parks have a 10 p.m. curfew and trails are dawn to dusk. Permitted events, field reservations, gates and maintenance can control the plateau independently.
belmont-plateau.restrooms: Do not count on a permanently open restroom at the overlook. Restroom access may be tied to an event, permitted field or seasonal facility, so confirm before settling in for a long picnic.
belmont-plateau.fees: Ordinary overlook, lawn and trail access is free. Ticketed festivals, permitted gatherings, vendors and reserved sports use are separate.
belmont-plateau.accessibility: The primary arrival reaches a broad open plateau, but grass, slopes, curb transitions, event barriers and natural-surface trail connections vary. Confirm the event layout when visiting during a festival.
belmont-plateau.dogs: Leashed dogs may use ordinary open park areas under the City's six-foot leash rule. Keep pets out of active fields, event-controlled areas and any posted animal-free zones.
belmont-plateau.family: The skyline view and open lawn work for a picnic or short family stop, but this is not a fenced playground. Bring shade and water, supervise near roads and fields, and verify restroom availability.
belmont-plateau.need: Belmont Plateau changes character during major festivals and sports events. Check the City event calendar, road restrictions and weather before relying on a normal parking or picnic setup.

fairmount-water-works.description: Fairmount Water Works is the free watershed education center and historic riverfront complex below the Philadelphia Museum of Art, with exhibits and outdoor Schuylkill views.
fairmount-water-works.location: Navigate to 640 Waterworks Drive below the art museum. The entrance is at river level beside the Schuylkill, not at the Rocky Steps or the upper museum plaza.
fairmount-water-works.parking: The operator lists free two-hour parking along Waterworks Drive. Spaces and vehicle access can change for events, flooding and road closures, so use SEPTA, PHLASH or a backup garage when the riverfront is busy.
fairmount-water-works.hours: The interpretive center is open Wednesday through Saturday, 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Outdoor riverfront paths may be accessible more broadly, but exhibits, restrooms and staff follow building hours.
fairmount-water-works.restrooms: Use visitor facilities during interpretive-center hours. Do not assume the building is open on Sunday through Tuesday or after 5 p.m. simply because the river path is accessible.
fairmount-water-works.fees: General admission is free and donations are welcome. Groups of 10 or more must schedule in advance, with recommended group and tour donations published by the operator.
fairmount-water-works.accessibility: The operator currently reports no elevator access because of Hurricane Ida flood damage. Contact Water Works before a visit requiring elevator service or a specific exhibit route.
fairmount-water-works.dogs: Pets are not a normal fit inside the interpretive center. Leashed dogs may use ordinary outdoor park paths where posted; confirm service-animal access with the operator.
fairmount-water-works.family: The turbine, watershed exhibits, short film and river setting can make a strong free family stop. Confirm the Wednesday-Saturday schedule and elevator limitation before arriving with a stroller or mobility need.
fairmount-water-works.need: Separate the free exhibits from the outdoor riverfront. Building access is limited to Wednesday-Saturday, and the elevator remains unavailable; flooding or city events can also affect Waterworks Drive.

smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.description: Smith Memorial Playground and Playhouse is a free 6.5-acre family destination with more than 50 outdoor play structures, a three-level indoor Playhouse and the Ann Newman Giant Wooden Slide.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.location: Navigate to 3500 Reservoir Drive in East Fairmount Park. Smith is about one-third mile inside the park from the 33rd Street and Oxford Street transit approach.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.parking: A free lot sits in front of the Playhouse. When it fills, the operator allows parking along Reservoir Drive; remove valuables and obey all posted restrictions.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.hours: April-September: Tuesday-Friday 10 a.m.-6 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-7 p.m. October-March: Tuesday-Sunday 10 a.m.-5 p.m. Closed Mondays; weather may close all or part, and the Playhouse closes one hour before the Playground in spring and summer.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.restrooms: Restrooms are available as part of the staffed Playground and Playhouse visit. Do not rely on them before opening, after closing or during a weather closure.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.fees: Daily family visits are free. Advance reservations and fees apply to groups of more than 10 children, and rentals or special events are separate.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.accessibility: Smith describes inclusive indoor and outdoor play, but equipment and terrain vary by age and ability. Contact staff before visiting for a specific mobility, sensory or accommodation need.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.dogs: Animals are not permitted at Smith. ADA-defined service animals are welcome.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.family: Smith is designed especially for children age 10 and under. Children must remain with an adult, use age-appropriate equipment and stay within sight of their caregiver.
smith-memorial-playground-and-playhouse.need: Hours are weather permitting, the Playhouse can close before the outdoor playground, and food options nearby are limited. Bring food if needed, but grilling and barbecuing are prohibited.

shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.description: Shofuso is a ticketed 1.2-acre Japanese house and garden in West Fairmount Park, with timed entry, delicate historic interiors and separate visitor rules.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.address: Lansdowne Drive and Horticultural Drive, Philadelphia, PA 19131
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.sourceLabel: Japan America Society of Greater Philadelphia
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.location: Use the Shofuso pin inside the Centennial District near Lansdowne and Horticultural Drives. It is not the Horticulture Center entrance or the Please Touch Museum lot.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.parking: The operator lists free parking in the nearby lot. Capacity can tighten during Centennial District events, so reserve the timed visit before driving across the park.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.hours: Open Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m.-5 p.m. Entry is by timed ticket and capacity is limited; Shofuso operates rain or shine.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.restrooms: Plan restroom use around the staffed visit and nearby Centennial District facilities. Confirm current access when reserving, especially for a mobility or family need.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.fees: Published admission is $15 for adults and $10 for seniors, children 5-17, college students and teachers. SNAP/EBT and ACCESS admission is $2 for the cardholder plus up to four family members; listed member, military and museum-worker categories are free.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.accessibility: The operator says the historic house is not wheelchair or scooter accessible and is not easily accessible for walkers, canes or prosthetics. Rubber-tipped or softly covered mobility devices are permitted inside; contact staff before booking.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.dogs: Do not expect pets inside the house or garden. Confirm service-animal access and any accommodation directly before purchasing a timed ticket.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.family: The garden can be memorable for children who can move carefully around water, plants and fragile interiors. Timed capacity, house rules and the major mobility limitation should shape the visit.
shofuso-japanese-cultural-center.need: Reserve a timed ticket; capacity is limited and ordinary photoshoots are not permitted during open hours. The site is open rain or shine, but the historic house has significant mobility barriers.

please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.description: Please Touch Museum is the ticketed children's museum inside Memorial Hall, with interactive exhibits, a historic carousel, two floors of visitor services and its own parking and schedule.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.address: 4231 Avenue of the Republic, Philadelphia, PA 19131
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.location: Navigate to Memorial Hall at 4231 Avenue of the Republic in West Fairmount Park. The museum is separate from Shofuso, the Horticulture Center and Belmont Plateau even though all are in the Centennial District.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.parking: Use the museum's gated lot beside Memorial Hall and check the current parking charge when reserving. Designated accessible spaces are in the adjacent museum lot.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.hours: Closed Monday and Tuesday. Open Wednesday-Saturday 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; first, fourth and fifth Sundays 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; second and third Sundays 11 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Holiday and special-event hours differ, so verify the selected date.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.restrooms: Restrooms are available on both museum floors, with baby-changing stations in select restrooms. A nursing room is on the lower level behind the Creative Arts Studio.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.fees: Admission is ticketed, and reservations are encouraged for visitors and members age 12 months and older. Use the museum's current reservation page for admission, carousel and parking prices rather than an older listing.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.accessibility: The museum documents accessible parking, restrooms on both floors, a nursing room and sensory and accommodation programs. One complimentary personal-care-attendant admission is available on request for an eligible paid visitor or member.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.dogs: ADA-defined service animals are welcome. Emotional-support, comfort and therapy animals are not permitted inside.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.family: This is a purpose-built children's museum with interactive exhibits and a carousel. Reserve ahead, check the day's opening time and build in breaks for food, restrooms and sensory needs.
please-touch-museum-and-memorial-hall.need: Sunday opening time changes by week of the month, and holidays or events can override the weekly schedule. Make a reservation for faster entry and confirm current admission, carousel and parking charges.
